memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He is to examine the mould on the walls, and if it has greenish or reddish depressions that appear to be deeper than the surface of the wall, the priest shall go out the doorway of the house and close it up for seven days. On the seventh day the priest shall return to inspect the house. If the mould has spread on the walls, he is to order that the contaminated stones be torn out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town." - Lev 14:37-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same patient pattern we saw with skin. Examine. Close it up. Come back in seven days. And if it has spread, act decisively.

But look at the phrase deeper than the surface of the wall. This is the question that has run through both chapters. Is this on the surface, or has it got into the structure?

Every household knows the difference. There are surface problems — a disagreement, a hard week, a bad mood. And there are structural ones — a pattern of harshness, a marriage where honesty has quietly died, a home where God's Word has not been opened in years. Surface problems can be wiped clean. Structural ones must be dug out.

Notice what happens when it goes deep: the stones come out. Not painted over. Not covered with a picture. Torn out and carried away.

That is costly, and it leaves a hole in the wall. But leaving contaminated stones in place because removal is disruptive is how a house is eventually lost.

Ask honestly about your home. Is there something you have been decorating over rather than removing? God gives grace for the disruption of doing it properly.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your home life is structural rather than surface?
2. What have you been covering over rather than removing?
3. What would it take to deal with it properly this month?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, show me what in my home has gone deeper than the surface. Give me courage to remove what needs removing rather than decorating over it. Amen.
